title: Build an assistant that knows when to stop
outcome: Implement a bounded workflow with explicit stopping reasons.
story: Amina’s assistant can look up an order, retrieve a policy, and draft a reply. If it cannot finish, it should explain why instead of looping or trying unapproved actions.

frames.explanation: One allowed operation consumes one step.
The workflow stops at a write boundary. A model proposal cannot bypass the application.

sections.title: Write a workflow before adding an agent
paragraphs: A workflow describes the permitted states and transitions: receive a question, retrieve evidence, draft, validate, and finish or escalate. Start with a deterministic sequence when it meets the need.

An agent may choose an action based on model output. That choice adds uncertainty, so keep a small registry of permitted actions and a clear controller. Separate the controller from the model and tool adapters so the controller can be tested without a paid model call.

sections.title: Make stopping states visible
paragraphs: Use distinct completion, waiting, budget, approval, failed, and unknown-action states. The caller needs to know whether there is an answer, missing information, or required human action. Do not report a stopped workflow as a completed answer.
The lab processes prepared event names. lookup consumes one step; done completes; write requires approval; error fails. It is a controller exercise, not evidence of an autonomous model’s performance.

sections.title: Limit more than step count
paragraphs: Set maximum steps, elapsed time, provider tokens or cost, tool calls, retries, and repeated identical actions. Check limits before an operation and account for its actual result afterward. A retry is another operation.

Keep tool execution under server permissions. Validate the proposed action at every iteration. A stop condition must terminate work, including delayed responses and pending operations, rather than merely change a label in the interface.

sections.title: Test the worst transitions
paragraphs: Reproduce repeated lookup, malformed action, provider failure, approval change, timeout, and duplicate completion. Check both the reported state and the actual tool calls. A budget label is incorrect if another tool executes afterward.

For a real provider run, save a safe trace of chosen actions and outcomes without exposing private messages or credentials. Use those traces to add regression cases and compare whether an agent improves on the fixed workflow.

words.meaning: Application code that decides which state and operation may follow.
The maximum number of allowed operations in a run.
A state from which the current run performs no further work.

example.code:
function run(events,limit){if(!Number.isInteger(limit)||limit<0)throw new RangeError("Invalid step limit");let used=0;for(const event of events){if(used>=limit)return {state:"budget",used};if(event==="done")return {state:"done",used};if(event==="write")return {state:"approval",used};if(event==="error")return {state:"failed",used};if(event!=="lookup")return {state:"unknown",used};used++;}return {state:"waiting",used};}
console.log(run(["lookup","write","lookup"],3));
explanation: The write proposal stops at approval.
The final lookup is never processed.

exercise.title: A bounded event controller
exercise.brief: Write run(events,limit). Process lookup, done, write, error. Check the step budget before each event. Invalid limits raise RangeError; unknown events stop. Return state and used.

steps.title: Track work and completion
steps.task: lookup increments used. done returns done immediately. An exhausted event list returns waiting.
steps.hint: Use an early return to ensure later events are not processed.
steps.solution: function run(events,limit){let used=0;for(const event of events){if(event==="done")return {state:"done",used};used++;}return {state:"waiting",used};}

steps.title: Stop at the budget
steps.task: Before each event, stop with budget if used >= limit.
steps.hint: Put the check before processing the next event.
steps.solution: function run(events,limit){let used=0;for(const event of events){if(used>=limit)return {state:"budget",used};if(event==="done")return {state:"done",used};used++;}return {state:"waiting",used};}

steps.title: Handle unsafe and failed transitions
steps.task: write returns approval, error returns failed, unknown events return unknown. Reject invalid limits.
steps.hint: These stops do not consume or execute a lookup.
steps.solution: function run(events,limit){if(!Number.isInteger(limit)||limit<0)throw new RangeError("Invalid step limit");let used=0;for(const event of events){if(used>=limit)return {state:"budget",used};if(event==="done")return {state:"done",used};if(event==="write")return {state:"approval",used};if(event==="error")return {state:"failed",used};if(event!=="lookup")return {state:"unknown",used};used++;}return {state:"waiting",used};}

cases.label: No available budget
cases.why: Check the bound before processing even a completion event.

cases.label: A proposed write
cases.why: Writing requires a separate authorized flow.

cases.label: A failed operation
cases.why: A failure must not continue blindly.

project.title: A bounded shop assistant
project.brief: Implement a controller using the actual service tool adapters. Compare a fixed workflow with an optional model-chosen workflow and keep their evaluation evidence separate.
deliverables: A controller with step, time, and cost limits.
Tests proving no operations run after stopping.

milestones.title: Define the flow
actions: Choose a fixed sequence as the baseline.

milestones.title: Add real adapters
actions: Use scoped order lookup and policy retrieval.

milestones.title: Prove termination
actions: Count actual tool invocations in tests.
Reproduce repeated actions, timeout, and provider failure.
Assert that terminal states execute no later operations.

acceptance: All actions pass a tool registry.
Approval and permissions remain server enforced.
Tests inspect actual calls after stopping.

tests.expected: The run stops within its limit.
No simulated money changes before approval.

project.extension: Persist a resumable run and prevent an expired approval from being reused after recovery.
reflection: Why begin with a fixed workflow?
How did you prove that stop actually stopped?
